q: My Linux server is running slowly. Find the process consuming the most CPU, display its PID, user, CPU and memory usage, check which files it has open, and show how to terminate it gracefully.

steps.what: busiest process with pid, user, cpu, memory

q: My root partition is 95% full. Identify the largest directories under /var, find files larger than 500 MB modified in the last seven days, exclude mounted filesystems, and show how to identify which files can safely be removed.

steps.what: files over 500 MB changed in the last 7 days, same filesystem

q: Search /var/log for the 20 most frequent error messages from the last 24 hours, ignore case, exclude lines containing 'health check', and display each message with its count in descending order.

My application on port 8080 is unreachable. Check whether anything is listening on that port, identify the owning process, test connectivity locally, inspect relevant firewall rules, and provide commands to diagnose the problem without changing system configuration.

steps.what: what listens on 8080 and which process owns it

q: Create a compressed backup of /home/app/data, preserve permissions and timestamps, exclude cache directories and .tmp files, save it with the current date in its filename, and verify the archive can be listed afterward.

steps.what: create the compressed archive with exclusions
list the archive to verify it

q: Find .log files under /var/log/myapp that are older than 30 days and larger than 100 MB. First show the matching files and their sizes, then provide a separate command to delete only those files.

steps.what: show the matching files without deleting

q: A service runs as user appuser but receives 'Permission denied' when accessing /srv/app/config.yaml. Inspect the file and parent-directory permissions, identify the file owner and group, and suggest the smallest permission change that would grant access without making the file world-readable.

steps.what: permissions of the file and its parent directories

q: My Python web application works when started manually but fails after reboot under systemd. Inspect the service status and logs, check the configured working directory and environment, verify the Python executable path, and suggest diagnostic commands before changing the service.

Given a CSV file containing timestamp, IP address, HTTP status, and response time, extract requests from the last hour with status codes 500-599, group them by IP, count failures, calculate the average response time, and display the top 10 IPs by failure count.

A Linux server has high CPU usage, low available memory, and a rapidly growing application log. Without rebooting or installing packages, identify the top five CPU-consuming processes, find the largest log files modified in the last 24 hours, check whether the application is repeatedly restarting under systemd, and provide a prioritized diagnosis plan. Do not execute any destructive commands.

steps.what: largest log files changed in the last 24 hours
